handoff.summary: Batch b03 curates 3 records: latent-heat phase-change magnitude, refrigerator cooling COP at an operating point, and the Carnot heating-COP bound. Complements b01 (sensible/slab/R) and b02 (heating COP, HSPF, Rth, mass) with no resubmission.

assumptions: source assumption: complete isothermal phase change at the transition temperature with no temperature change until the change is complete; energy scales with mass and bond strength via an experimentally determined coefficient (OpenStax 14.3).
Same sample, substance, transition (fusion or vaporization pair), and constant-temperature condition for m, L, and Q; L treated as constant for the stated transition.
Magnitude semantics: Q is the nonnegative energy for the stated direction; freezing/condensation release has the same magnitude with reversed flow direction handled outside this record.

gaps: Requires extensions: mass (kg, reuses b01/b02 mass), latent_heat_coefficient (J/kg), latent_heat_transfer (J). No runtime unit fits L or Q in J.
Magnitude-only record: sign/direction of freezing vs melting and condensation vs vaporization needs an application adapter, not a silent sign flip.

models.inverse_notes: Q with positive L gives m=Q/L; Q with positive m gives L=Q/m. Zero mass or zero coefficient excluded. Substitution checked: Q=334000, L=334000 gives m=1.0 kg. Inversion does not establish transition direction or completeness.
limitations: Excludes sensible heating/cooling before or after the transition (needs the b01 sensible-heat record) and partial-change or sub-boiling evaporation regimes with higher effective energy.
Table coefficients are representatives for the stated transition, not defaults for any sample or condition.

references.method: Published result: source evaluates Q=(1.0 kg)(334 kJ/kg)=334 kJ for melting 1 kg ice at 0C; stored as 334000 J. Replay exact; tolerance 500 J covers the 3-significant kJ display rounding (half unit 0.5 kJ).
references.provenance: Published textbook evaluation with kJ-to-J conversion

references.method: Published result: source states 2256 kJ vaporizes 1 kg water at 100C; stored as 2256000 J. Replay exact; tolerance 500 J covers display rounding. Materially different transition from the fusion case.
references.provenance: Published textbook evaluation with kJ-to-J conversion (vaporization branch)

rejection_cases.reason: Zero mass ceases to describe a sample; guard m>0 rejects it (no ideal zero-mass boundary for this definition).
Latent coefficient L is required; mass alone does not determine phase-change heat.

relationship.locator: Sec. 14.3, Eqs. 14.17-14.18 with Table 14.2 coefficients and 1-kg water evaluations (334 kJ melt, 2256 kJ vaporize)
relationship.original_equation: Q = mLf (melting/freezing, Eq. 14.17); Q = mLv (vaporization/condensation, Eq. 14.18)
relationship.translation_notes: Generic L renames Lf/Lv for the stated transition (fusion or vaporization) to keep one canonical record; complete isothermal change only. Units: m in kg, L in J/kg, Q in J. Dimensional check: kg*(J/kg)=J (energy). Magnitude semantics retained; no temperature-change term.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: phase-change heat is Q=mLf for melting/freezing and Q=mLv for vaporization/condensation with experimentally determined coefficients in J/kg; 1 kg ice at 0C needs 334 kJ to melt (same as heating 1 kg water 0C to 79.8C) and 1 kg water at 100C needs 2256 kJ to vaporize; soda-ice example uses mice*Lf=0.018*334000=6012 J.

Heating/cooling pair linked by COPref=COP_hp-1 under Qh=Qc+W; that relation is noted, not separately curated.

models.inverse_notes: Qc and positive COPref give W=Qc/COPref; W and COPref give Qc=COPref*W. Zero Qc with positive W gives COPref 0 (degenerate). Substitution checked: Qc=4.3, W=1.0 gives 4.3; inversion W=4.3/4.3=1.0.
limitations: Excludes heating COP (separate b02 record), seasonal metrics, and EER in Btu/Wh; COPref=COP_hp-1 relates the two point records but is not curated as a separate model here.
Real units typically range 2-6 per source; Carnot values are ideal bounds, not defaults.

references.method: Source-backed derivation: heating Carnot example gives Qh=5.30W with W=1.0 and Qh=Qc+W implies Qc=4.30, so COPref=4.30 consistent with Eq. 15.44 (5.30-1). Tolerance 0.01 covers two-decimal rounding.
references.provenance: Derived from the published Carnot heating example via source-stated Qh=Qc+W; ideal bound, not a field measurement

references.method: Ordinary illustration inside the published real range 2-6; replay 3.0/1.0=3.0 exact.

assumptions: source assumption: reversed Carnot (reversible, adiabatic/isothermal, no dissipative/frictional losses) between steady reservoirs; COP=1/Eff with EffC=1-Tc/Th in absolute temperature (OpenStax 15.5).
Same reservoir pair and reversible cycle for Th, Tc, and COPmax; Th and Tc are absolute kelvins, not Celsius readings or differences.
Ideal bound scope: best-possible performance at stated reservoirs; actual placement needs working-fluid temperatures beyond indoor/outdoor air (source strategy note).

gaps: Requires extensions: absolute temperatures in K (offset scale, not differences) and dimensionless Carnot-bound meaning. Must not be coerced to temperature_difference or point_heating_cop values.
Working-fluid vs air temperature placement and unit-rating procedures need separate records.

models.inverse_notes: Th and Tc strictly ordered positive absolutes; Th>Tc excludes equality. With COPmax and Tc, Th=COPmax*(Th-Tc) solves as Th=COPmax*Tc/(COPmax-1) requiring COPmax>1; with COPmax and Th, Tc=Th*(1-1/COPmax). Substitution checked: 5.3 and Tc=258 give Th=5.3*258/4.3=318.0 within rounding. Bound inversion does not make real units reversible.
limitations: Ideal upper bound only; real heating COP ranges about 2-4 and degrades in very cold climates (small-lift advantage reversed). Not a default efficiency.
Excludes refrigerator-bound form Tc/(Th-Tc), engine efficiency 1-Tc/Th as a separate record, and all irreversibilities, sizing, and cost considerations.

references.method: Published result: source computes EffC=1-258/318=0.1887 and COP=1/0.1887=5.30. Direct form 318/(318-258)=5.3 exact; tolerance 0.01 covers the reported two-decimal rounding.
Independent illustration of the same ideal bound at a materially different mild-lift pair: 300/30=10.0 exact, showing the small-difference advantage. Not a published example.
references.provenance: Independent elementary illustration of the source-stated bound form

rejection_cases.reason: Zero lift (Th=Tc) makes the bound singular and no heat-pumping lift exists; guard Th>Tc rejects it.
Cold reservoir Tc is required; one reservoir alone does not determine the bound.

relationship.locator: Sec. 15.5 Best-COP example, Eqs. 15.38-15.42 with Th=45.0C=318K, Tc=-15.0C=258K and small-difference discussion
relationship.translation_notes: Source-backed derivation combining COP=1/Eff with Carnot EffC=1-Tc/Th to single form Th/(Th-Tc); no new physics introduced. Units: Th, Tc absolute kelvins; result dimensionless. Dimensional check: temperature/temperature-difference = dimensionless (offset-free scale required; Celsius inputs invalid without conversion).

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: reversed Carnot gives best performance with COP=1/Eff and EffC=1-Tc/Th; for Th=318K and Tc=258K, EffC=0.1887 and COP=5.30 with Qh=5.30W; smaller hot-cold differences raise COP; friction reduces real COP to about 2-4.
